problem: A reviewer with several pull requests open holds the relationship between them in their head. The viewer reviews one pull request at a time, so nothing on screen answers the question the reviewer actually carries: do any of these fight each other, and should any of them be one review instead of two. GitHub's stacked pull requests answer a narrower version, because a stack is a parent-child chain the author declares in advance. The set a reviewer needs is assembled after the fact, out of work several people opened without coordinating.
why_now: The team wants to get through pull request reviews with more ease. The bundle already holds the material a relationship could be computed from, and the record index already resolves five other kinds of join. A pull-request-to-pull-request relationship is the one join nobody has built.
approach: The machine proposes, and the reviewer corrects. A terminal-side mode reads the selected pull requests, fetches their branches, and computes two things: an ordered list of contested regions, where a region is a file and a line span more than one pull request writes, and a proposed partition of the set into review units. The reviewer walks the regions with one keypress each, and corrects the partition with three gestures. Every keypress appends one line to the ledger through shared/ledger.py, with direct file access and no HTTP request. A projection folds those lines into one recorded call per pull request, and into the missing pull-request-to-pull-request join. The viewer renders the proposal and the recorded calls, and never computes them.

alternatives.option: The Gang Rail: shift-click the queue dots, stack one narration pane per selected pull request down the existing four levels, and swap the dock buttons
alternatives.rejected_because: It is the cheapest option and it only rearranges what the reviewer must read. It does no work on the reviewer's behalf. Its stacked panes are also empty for the exact cohort the deck serves, because both open pull requests carry no narration. Its shift-click multi-select is kept, as the mechanic for correcting a proposal.

alternatives.option: Contested Subjects: swap the level rail for cards of shared repo nouns, quoting each pull request verbatim, with a SILENT row where a pull request said nothing
alternatives.rejected_because: It renders evidence more honestly than any other option, and it still waits for the reviewer to assemble the set before it does anything. Its SILENT-row rule is kept as a rendering rule for the chosen approach, because absence must never render as agreement.

alternatives.option: The Claims Docket: one row per machine claim with its rule, its inputs, and a computed or unassessable basis, with the per-pull-request call derived from settled claims
alternatives.rejected_because: Ten of fourteen pull requests carry no authored intent, so the docket is mostly empty rows, and the build is four new subsystems, most of them inside viewer/index.html, which ADR-0020 already names as the repository's largest maintenance problem. Its unassessable row is kept, because a blind spot must appear on the record rather than be absent from it.

alternatives.option: Shared-path overlap from the touched map as an evidence level
alternatives.rejected_because: 86 of the 91 possible pairs share a path prefix, and (root) alone is shared by 12 of 14 pull requests. Presence of overlap is the base rate in this repository, not a finding. Only magnitude and specificity carry information.

alternatives.option: Compute the relationship in the browser and render it live
alternatives.rejected_because: The browser cannot run git, so it cannot see a textual conflict at all. ADR-0001 also holds the viewer to one self-contained file under a content policy that blocks every external request, so the browser cannot fetch the evidence either.

alternatives.option: Let the deck write to GitHub directly: retarget a base, close, merge
alternatives.rejected_because: It needs a credential inside a page that also publishes as a Claude Artifact, and it breaks the rule that the viewer is a static page served by python3 -m http.server.

alternatives.option: Record the call through the existing POST /feedback endpoint, as the comments drawer does
alternatives.rejected_because: That path works only under serve_bundle.py --allow-write. Plain http.server returns 404, and a published Artifact's content policy blocks the request. Both fall back to browser storage with a message promising a sync that nothing implements, so the call never reaches the mode meant to act on it. A terminal-side writer has direct file access and none of these failure modes.

alternatives.option: Rank the correction reasons by the reviewer's own precedent from day one
alternatives.rejected_because: The ledger is 0 bytes. The precedent table, the ranked reasons, and the counterfactual all read an empty file. The proposer works without history, because history improves the reason ranking and does not produce the partition. Deferred to a later epic.

alternatives.option: Take the input set from a live gh pr list
alternatives.rejected_because: It depends on the first epic of the inflight-record-store design, which is backlog and unbuilt. The set comes from data/story.json instead, and the deck reads one entity list, so that later work widens the input without a redesign.

out_of_scope: Every GitHub write. No merge, no close, no comment, no label, no reviewer, no base retarget.
The precedent engine, the reason ranking, and the counterfactual on a bracket boundary.
Any conflict computation inside the browser.
Renaming or restructuring the five existing view modes.
Fixing the design-level join in shared/build_index.py. Deferred to the inflight-record-store design, which owns the pull-request entity gap.
risks: The proposer must fetch the open branches before git merge-tree can say anything. This checkout holds master and one working branch, so a mode that has so far only read local git gains a network step.

Folding region verdicts with union-find is transitive. A reviewer who groups A with B at one region and B with C at another has not said that A and C belong together, and the projection would assert it.

Deferring the design-level join leaves the cold-start proposer with textual conflict as its only strong signal, and textual conflict needs a fetch. A cohort with no fetchable branch gets an empty proposal.
A proposed partition accepted in silence records a decision the reviewer never examined. That is the mechanic's value and its danger in the same line.
A region list is computed against the current head of each branch. A push invalidates it, and a stale stop list is worse than none, because it looks current.
The chosen approach does work before the reviewer arrives, which is the point, and it also means a wrong proposal is the first thing they read. An anchoring effect is likely and unmeasured.
testing: Nothing is built. The first check is the throwaway script named in the first epic: parse the hunk headers already stored in the eight cached diff files and print the region table for pull requests 11 and 12, which share 29 files. If the stop list is not materially shorter than the shared-file list, the central claim of the approach is false and the design stops.
reviewer_focus: Whether a proposed partition helps a reviewer or anchors them.
The union-find transitivity rule, and whether the projection should stop at pairwise edges.
Whether the viewer stays a pure renderer, with no relationship computed in the browser.
unknowns: Whether a stop list is materially shorter than a file list on a real cohort. Untested against anything.
Whether a reviewer corrects a wrong grouping more readily than they build a right one. This is the load-bearing claim of the approach and it rests on judgement, not measurement.
How a region list should behave when one branch of the set is pushed mid-review.
